title: Explain Types and Purposes of Audits and Assessments

sections.title: What You Are Learning
paragraphs: Organizations use audits, assessments, attestations, and penetration testing to gather evidence that security controls work. Some evaluations are performed internally, while others require an independent external review.
The key distinctions are who performs the evaluation, what the activity is meant to prove, and how much information or access a penetration tester receives.
sections.callout: Recognition goal: identify who is evaluating the organization, what is being evaluated, and how much the tester knows about the target.

entries.title: Attestation
paragraphs: A formal declaration or confirmation that stated requirements, conditions, or controls have been met. It provides assurance to management, customers, regulators, or other stakeholders.
entries.recognitionCue: Formal statement confirming compliance or control status -> attestation

sections.title: Internal Audits and Assessments
paragraphs: Internal activities are performed by or for the organization itself. They support improvement and oversight from inside the organization, but may not provide the same independence as an external review.

entries.title: Internal assessments
paragraphs: Evaluations performed by or for the organization itself.
entries.recognitionCue: The organization evaluates itself -> internal assessment

entries.title: Compliance assessment
paragraphs: An internal compliance review checks whether the organization follows its policies, standards, regulations, and contractual requirements.
entries.recognitionCue: The organization checks its own compliance -> compliance assessment

entries.title: Audit committee
paragraphs: A governance group that oversees audit activities and may review findings, risk, compliance issues, and remediation.
entries.recognitionCue: Governance group overseeing audits -> audit committee

entries.title: Self-assessments
paragraphs: Control or compliance evaluations performed by the responsible organization. They can lower cost, support frequent evaluation, and identify gaps early, but they have less independence than an external audit.
entries.recognitionCue: The organization grades itself -> self-assessment

sections.title: External Audits and Assessments
paragraphs: External evaluations are performed by parties outside the organization and provide outside or independent assurance.

entries.title: External assessments
paragraphs: Evaluations of security posture, controls, or compliance performed from outside the organization.
entries.recognitionCue: An outside evaluator reviews security posture -> external assessment

entries.title: Regulatory audit
paragraphs: An external review that evaluates whether the organization meets requirements established by an applicable regulator.
entries.recognitionCue: A regulator evaluates required compliance -> regulatory audit

entries.title: Examinations
paragraphs: Formal reviews of systems, controls, records, processes, or operations used to determine compliance or effectiveness.
entries.recognitionCue: Detailed formal review of records or controls -> examination

entries.title: Assessment
paragraphs: An outside evaluation of security condition, controls, or compliance.
entries.recognitionCue: Outside evaluator reviews security condition or compliance -> assessment

entries.title: Independent third-party audit
paragraphs: An objective audit performed by an unaffiliated outside organization. Independence can provide stronger assurance to external stakeholders.
entries.recognitionCue: An independent outside auditor evaluates the organization -> third-party audit

table.caption: Internal and external evaluation distinction
rows: An outside party evaluates the organization
An unaffiliated outside auditor provides stronger independence

sections.title: Penetration Testing
paragraphs: Penetration testing is an authorized attempt to identify and exploit security weaknesses. Unlike an audit that evaluates controls or compliance, a penetration test actively tests defenses.

entries.title: Penetration testing
paragraphs: Authorized attempts to identify and exploit security weaknesses.
entries.recognitionCue: Actively test defenses under authorization -> penetration testing

entries.title: Physical penetration test
paragraphs: Evaluates physical-security controls such as doors, locks, badges, barriers, and facility access.
entries.recognitionCue: Test physical access controls -> physical penetration test

entries.title: Offensive penetration test
paragraphs: The testing team acts like an adversary and focuses on attacking or exploiting defenses.
entries.recognitionCue: Simulated attacker activity -> offensive penetration test

entries.title: Defensive penetration test
paragraphs: Focuses on whether defenders can detect, respond to, and stop simulated attack activity.
entries.recognitionCue: Evaluate defensive capabilities -> defensive penetration test

entries.title: Integrated penetration test
paragraphs: Evaluates offensive and defensive teams together: one side attacks while the other detects and responds.
entries.recognitionCue: Offense and defense operate in the same exercise -> integrated penetration test

sections.title: Knowledge Levels
paragraphs: The amount of information provided to a penetration tester changes the style of the assessment.

entries.title: Known environment
paragraphs: The tester receives extensive information about the target, such as architecture, credentials, source information, or configuration details.
entries.recognitionCue: High level of internal target knowledge -> known environment

entries.title: Partially known environment
paragraphs: The tester receives some information about the target, but still must discover the rest.
entries.recognitionCue: Some target knowledge and some discovery -> partially known environment

entries.title: Unknown environment
paragraphs: The tester receives little or no internal information and must discover the environment similarly to an external attacker.
entries.recognitionCue: Little or no internal target knowledge -> unknown environment

sections.title: Reconnaissance
paragraphs: Reconnaissance gathers information about a target before or during testing. The key distinction is whether the tester directly interacts with the target environment.

entries.title: Reconnaissance
paragraphs: Collection of information about a target before or during a test.
entries.recognitionCue: Gather target information before or during testing -> reconnaissance

entries.title: Passive reconnaissance
paragraphs: Gathers information, including publicly available information, without directly interacting with target systems.
entries.recognitionCue: Learn about the target without touching its systems -> passive reconnaissance

entries.title: Active reconnaissance
paragraphs: Directly interacts with the target environment by probing hosts, services, or network resources.
entries.recognitionCue: Interact with or probe target systems -> active reconnaissance

sections.title: Recognition Cues
bullets: Formal declaration that requirements or controls are met = attestation
The organization evaluates itself = internal assessment or self-assessment
Internal review against requirements = compliance assessment
Governance oversight of audits = audit committee
Regulator performs the review = regulatory audit
Formal inspection of records or controls = examination
Unaffiliated outside auditor = independent third-party audit
Test physical barriers or facility access = physical penetration test
Simulated attacker = offensive; test defenders = defensive; test both together = integrated
Extensive information = known; some information = partially known; little or none = unknown
No direct target interaction = passive reconnaissance; direct probing = active reconnaissance

sections.title: Objective 5.5 Exam Trap
paragraphs: Do not confuse an audit with a penetration test. An audit evaluates controls or compliance, while a penetration test actively attempts exploitation. Also separate who performs an evaluation from how much a penetration tester knows: internal and external identify the evaluator, while known, partially known, and unknown identify the tester's target knowledge.
sections.callout: Ask who is performing the assessment, what is being tested, and how much information the tester has.

sections.title: Maestro Recognition Sheet
bullets: Try to enter a facility = physical penetration test

miniCheck.intro: Classify the test conditions and information-gathering method.
miniCheck.prompt: An authorized penetration-testing team receives network diagrams and selected system details, but not complete target information. The team then probes hosts and services to discover what is reachable.

fields.label: Reconnaissance method used to probe the target

miniCheck.correctFeedback: Correct. The team has some but not complete target information, so the environment is partially known. Probing target hosts and services is active reconnaissance because it directly interacts with the environment.
miniCheck.retryFeedback: Not quite. First decide how much target information the testers received, then decide whether their information gathering directly touched the target systems.
